examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Design states around the information about the processed prefix that future input needs. Provide a transition for every state-symbol pair, including a rejecting sink if needed. For modular counts/products, prove that your tracked residue is sufficient and then prove state minimality separately.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
What is the minimum number of DFA states for binary strings whose length is divisible by 4?

**Answer: 4.** Track length modulo 4 with residues 0,1,2,3. Either symbol advances by one modulo 4; residue 0 is start/final. A suffix completing one residue to 0 distinguishes it from the others, so four states are necessary.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Accepting a prefix does not guarantee later acceptance. An accepting state need not be a sink.

An accepting state is not necessarily a stopping state; the remaining input must still be consumed.
